- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (especially +0.36+ sentiment) — model tends to overshoot and then correct.
- Underestimate when sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., -1.25 or below) — model fails to anticipate sharp reversals or mean reversion.
- Lag in response to recent price drops — model often holds too much of the prior trend, missing immediate reversal signals.
- Overreact to short-term sentiment volatility — model amplifies sentiment-driven moves, especially in 30-day horizon.
- Mean reversion bias: model overweights recent highs and underweights lows — correct by smoothing out extreme recent values.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, model tends to overpredict — reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to recent mean.
- Avoid extrapolating from 18-day history — model overfits to recent data, especially when sentiment is trending. Use 30-day moving average as anchor.
